active_paradigms.idea: Solve an exact set-partitioning formulation with scipy.optimize.milp over feasible GPU configurations
active_paradigms.description: The current program uses pressure-aware list scheduling: models are ordered by standalone pressure, each is placed on the GPU giving the lexicographically smallest sorted KVPR vector, and then at most five best-improving one-model moves or pairwise swaps are applied. Its strength is that it evaluates the true ratio objective for every tested greedy choice and preserves memory feasibility, but it can become trapped because the initial irreversible ordering and shallow neighborhood cannot perform coordinated rearrangements. For small or moderate model counts, enumerate every subset of models whose total model_size is at most 80 GB; each subset is a feasible configuration for one GPU, with a precomputed configuration KVPR equal to sum(req_rate/slo)/(80-sum(model_size)). Create one binary variable per configuration and use scipy.optimize.milp to select exactly gpu_num configurations while requiring every model to occur in exactly one selected configuration; include the empty configuration so unused GPUs are represented. Introduce a scalar z and impose z >= configuration_kvpr * selected_configuration for every configuration, then minimize z, which directly minimizes the testcase maximum KVPR rather than a proxy. This is globally optimal over the enumerated configuration set and attacks precisely the multi-model coordination missing from moves and swaps. The supplied wrapper only shows that evaluation delegates to evaluator.py, while the stated objective indicates each testcase placement should independently minimize its own maximum KVPR; no cross-test state should be retained.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Directly minimize each testcase's maximum GPU KVPR, which lowers the mean max-KVPR before the evaluator takes its reciprocal score transformation.
active_paradigms.cautions: Subset enumeration is exponential, so use this only when len(models) is sufficiently small or when model sizes permit aggressive pruning of infeasible subsets. Do not use rounded model sizes when checking the real 80 GB limit; the returned selected subsets must preserve exact model objects. Configurations with zero remaining memory have infinite pressure when they have positive load and should be excluded or assigned a prohibitively large coefficient. Ensure the MILP result is checked for success and retain a feasible greedy fallback if enumeration would be too large.

active_paradigms.idea: Use scipy.optimize.differential_evolution with integer GPU-label variables and exact nonlinear memory constraints
active_paradigms.description: Represent a placement by one integer variable per model, whose value is its GPU index, and evaluate it by recomputing every GPU's used memory, request load, and exact maximum KVPR. Unlike the current deterministic greedy construction, scipy.optimize.differential_evolution can change many assignments at once and therefore cross the local barriers that require several temporarily non-improving moves. Use its integrality argument so the search variables remain GPU labels, and impose one scipy.optimize.NonlinearConstraint per GPU requiring 80 minus that GPU's assigned total model_size to be nonnegative. The objective should be the maximum finite load/remaining-memory ratio, with a very large value for any infeasible or zero-denominator loaded GPU. Break GPU-label permutation symmetry by pinning a deterministic anchor model to GPU 0 or by canonicalizing labels inside objective evaluation; this avoids wasting most of the population on equivalent placements. Seed the initial population around the current pressure-aware greedy result plus diversified perturbations, so the existing strong heuristic remains useful while the global population search explores qualitatively different partitions. This is a direct discrete placement search, not tuning the parameters of another algorithm.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Escape the current five-iteration move/swap local optimum and optimize the actual maximum-ratio objective under exact memory constraints.
active_paradigms.cautions: This can be slower than the greedy method, especially with many models, so set a bounded population size and iteration budget consistent with evaluator time limits. Objective evaluation must tolerate empty GPUs, whose pressure is zero, and must never divide by a nonpositive residual capacity. Integer-label evolutionary search has substantial symmetry; failure to canonicalize or anchor labels can make it less reliable than the present heuristic. Return the best feasible decoded assignment only, not the floating optimizer vector.

active_paradigms.idea: Expand local search to exact multi-model ejection chains enumerated with itertools.combinations
active_paradigms.description: The present local search considers only a single relocation or a swap of one model on each side, accepts only strict immediate improvements, and repeats only min(5, number_of_models) times. Its greedy initialization is already effective because it compares the complete sorted KVPR profile, so a focused stronger neighborhood is likely simpler and safer than replacing all of it. Starting from that placement, enumerate small subsets of one to three models from the currently worst-pressure GPU using itertools.combinations, and test relocating that subset jointly to one or several destination GPUs whenever all destination memory constraints remain feasible. Also enumerate exchange chains such as worst GPU -> A, A -> B, B -> worst GPU, where each chain can exchange total size and total request weight in ways impossible for a pairwise swap. For every feasible candidate, recompute all changed GPUs' exact KVPRs and compare the full sorted pressure tuple, retaining the single lexicographically best strict improvement. Repeat until no improving chain exists rather than stopping after five rounds; accepting only strict tuple improvement guarantees termination and never degrades the primary maximum. This specifically repairs the current program's principal weakness: it cannot free enough memory on a desirable GPU to accept a high-load model unless every intermediate single move is beneficial and feasible.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Reduce the bottleneck GPU's KVPR through coordinated, memory-feasible reassignment while retaining the current algorithm's exact objective comparison and deterministic behavior.
active_paradigms.cautions: Cap subset size at two or three and prioritize models from the worst one or two GPUs, otherwise combinatorial enumeration can exceed the evaluation budget. Apply and undo aggregate size/load deltas carefully; the current swap bookkeeping is delicate, and chain evaluation is safer if it uses copied aggregate arrays or a single centralized delta routine. Reject candidates with residual memory at or below zero when their resulting load is positive. Preserve model identity when updating placement lists, particularly if model objects have equal attributes.
